blindSourceSummaries: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time; the underlying source is an international human-rights organisation's March 2026 statement on this country's transgender-person-rights amendment bill, characterising it as a major setback to the 2014 highest-court self-identification right and the 2019 law's protections.

A public broadcaster's report (26 March 2026) on the amendment bill narrowing trans self-identification, passed by both chambers and pending the head of state's assent: it limits recognition to intersex variations and traditional community identities certified by medical boards, makes board certification mandatory for gender-affirming surgery, and sparked protests; the highest court-appointed advisory panel asked the government to withdraw it, and critics including trans-rights activists warn it excludes many trans, non-binary and gender-fluid people.

A national daily (18 August 2024): a trans woman travelling to a medical college protest alleges a railway-police constable groped her at a metro station as a 'gender check'; police denied it and filed a counter-complaint. Shared national source: it evidences the policing practice of treating trans appearance as a suspicion category, which recurs in checkpoints and transit spaces countrywide rather than in this state/province specifically.
